claims.text: Premelting onset and overall melting behavior in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles are governed by the degree of surface segregation.
A homogeneously mixed CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticle has higher surface cohesive energy because of its high configurational entropy.
Surface enrichment by atoms with lower bonding energies lowers the nanoparticle surface energy.
Lower surface energy caused by segregation leads to earlier local structural disorder and premelting.
A refined post-synthesis anneal using shorter durations and lower temperatures can induce controlled surface segregation while minimizing sintering and morphology changes.
XPS, atom probe tomography, and high-resolution TEM can quantify elemental segregation at nanoparticle surfaces.
High configurational entropy stabilizes a uniform distribution of constituent atoms in CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles.
Surface segregation concentrates atoms having lower bonding energies or lower elemental melting points at the nanoparticle surface.
Concentration of such atoms at the surface reduces local cohesive energy.
Reduced local cohesive energy accelerates premelting and the onset of structural disorder during heating.
Surface-segregated nanoparticles will begin premelting earlier than compositionally homogeneous nanoparticles.
Premelting onset will be observable as an exothermic DSC event.
Premelting will be accompanied by amorphization or lattice disorder visible by in situ TEM.
Surface-segregated nanoparticles will exhibit a broader melting transition than homogeneous nanoparticles.
Homogeneous nanoparticles with minimal surface segregation will melt more uniformly, at higher temperatures, and with a sharper transition than segregated nanoparticles.

The proposed segregation-dependent behavior will hold across equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticle sizes from 5 to 20 nm under inert atmospheres and heating rates of 5–10 °C/min up to 0.9 times the bulk melting point.
Annealing may induce morphology changes other than surface segregation and thereby confound the comparison.
